sources.title: Solution to the ghost problem in higher-derivative gravity

evidence.text: The positive-energy wavefunction grows on the real z axis. The construction continues z into normalizable complex Stokes wedges, sets y=−iz and q=i pz, and applies a further non-unitary similarity transformation generated by a Hermitian Q to obtain an ordinary positive oscillator.

sources.title: Solution to the ghost problem in higher-derivative gravity

evidence.text: Spatial modes are reduced to the Pais–Uhlenbeck oscillator with omega_i=sqrt(spatial momentum squared+Mi^2), z replacing phi, and x=zdot. Ostrogradski or Dirac-constraint methods give its canonical two-oscillator Hamiltonian.

sources.title: Solution to the ghost problem in higher-derivative gravity

evidence.text: A fermion functional integral is used to motivate an induced term proportional to R_mu_nu R^mu_nu−R^2/3, with a logarithmically divergent coefficient. This is presented as a route from locally conformal matter to a fourth-order gravitational action.

sources.title: Ostrogradsky's Theorem is Incompatible with Background Independence in Quantum Gravity

evidence.text: Rewrite the classical gravitational equation as vanishing total energy-momentum tensor, then apply the metric Schwinger–Dyson identity to obtain ⟨√−g Tμν⟩=0. The author interprets this identity as the Hamiltonian and momentum constraints.

sources.title: Deformed General Relativity and Effective Actions from Loop Quantum Gravity

evidence.text: Extends algebraic reconstruction through a Legendre transform: vij = δH/δπij and L = πijvij−H. The constraint bracket becomes a functional equation for L, using the diffeomorphism constraint's linearity in momenta.

sources.title: Finite Conformal Quantum Gravity and Nonsingular Spacetimes

evidence.text: Harmonic-gauge propagator inversion and conserved-source residues test the Minkowski spectrum. Entire-function field redefinitions and unchanged Landau singularities/Cutkosky rules support the authors’ perturbative unitarity argument.

sources.title: Nakanishi–Kugo–Ojima quantization of general relativity in Heisenberg picture

evidence.text: Independent Palatini variations of w and e produce torsionlessness and the vacuum Einstein equation. A Legendre transform and covariant Poisson brackets then use (w,S) as phase-space variables.

evidence.text: Choose gauge connections as ensemble data, interpret system evolution as loop holonomy, and use the gauge action as the weight. This turns ensemble averaging into the ordinary functional integral for a single higher-dimensional theory with specified observable insertions.

evidence.text: Identify all independent scales, specify fixed couplings and discrete labels, nondimensionalize and compare dimensions. Apply the same common-scale cancellation to state-counting thresholds. In this paper the method concerns proposed quantum-break times and the emergence-motivated species count.

sources.title: Quantum Geometry and Black Holes

evidence.text: Parameterized Dirac observables represent gauge-dependent triads and metric components on the physical Hilbert space. Functional parameters select coordinates/slicings; the ordered-label observable Ô(z) supplies the radial triad, and the Hamiltonian constraint supplies Eφ.

sources.title: Conformal higher spin theory

evidence.text: Can covariance of a quantized point particle define an interacting conformal higher spin action whose low-spin truncation gives Weyl-invariant dilaton gravity and whose quadratic expansion contains every integer spin?

evidence.text: Can a quantum-gravity model with only global topological degrees of freedom and interactions defined through cobordisms generate a mass scale, a dynamical metric, and low-energy general relativity through gravitational instantons?

sources.title: Kinematics of arbitrary spin matter fields in loop quantum gravity

evidence.text: How do the Gauss and spatial diffeomorphism constraints shape arbitrary-spin matter coupled to loop quantum gravity, and how far can this quantum kinematics be derived from classical higher-spin actions?

sources.title: Making a Quantum Universe: Symmetry and Gravity

evidence.text: Can a background-free quantum Universe defined through infinite-dimensional symmetry account for universal quantum gravity, finite internal matter symmetries, and the origin of classical 3+1-dimensional spacetime?

sources.title: Swampland conjectures for an almost topological gravity theory

evidence.text: Does adding a propagating mode to topological dS gravity permit the quantum breaking proposed for graviton bound states? The paper contrasts the pure theory with the scalar-induced TMG phase and estimates only the dependence on the Hubble scale.

sources.title: Les Houches lectures on de Sitter space

evidence.text: Review classical de Sitter geometry, free scalar quantum field theory, horizon temperature and entropy as background for de Sitter quantum gravity; explain the conformal asymptotic symmetry underlying the proposed dS/CFT correspondence and derive suitable metric falloffs.

sources.title: AdS and the Swampland

evidence.text: Can quantum gravity admit families of effectively pure d-dimensional AdS vacua approaching flat space while retaining only finitely many light fields? The paper studies this question through varying cosmological constant, tower masses, and generalized field-space distance.

sources.title: Quantum field theory in curved space-time

evidence.text: These lectures review how quantum fields are interpreted on curved backgrounds, how gravitational fields create particles, how stress tensors are renormalized, what constrains negative energy, and where semiclassical gravity requires a fluctuating-metric description.

sources.title: Implication of the swampland distance conjecture on the Cohen–Kaplan–Nelson bound in de Sitter space

evidence.text: Can restrictions on global-symmetry restoration connect distance, weak-gravity, de Sitter, and CKN constraints?

sources.title: Covariant quantization of the partially massless graviton field in de Sitter spacetime

evidence.text: How can the partially massless spin-2 field be quantized covariantly on global de Sitter spacetime while accommodating gauge freedom and the absence of a global positive-energy spectral condition?

sources.title: Quantum Gravity as Gravitized Quantum Theory

evidence.text: Can phase-space regularization combined with holography motivate quantum gravity as quantum theory with dynamical state-space geometry and topology, and connect vacuum energy, experimental interference signatures, and particle mass hierarchies?

sources.title: A (Strictly) Contemporary Perspective on Trans-Planckian Censorship

evidence.text: Can a quantum field in an arbitrary state consistently source its curved background? The paper distinguishes field theory on a given globally hyperbolic geometry from the harder problem of self-consistent gravitational coupling.

sources.title: Keeping matter in the loop in dS$_{3}$ quantum gravity

evidence.text: How can massive matter be coupled to Chern-Simons dS3 quantum gravity while retaining calculability, and how does quantum gravity modify a scalar determinant and its inferred mass?

sources.title: Higher curvature counter terms cause the bounce in loop cosmology

evidence.text: Does the loop-cosmology bounce follow uniquely from quantization, or from an ambiguous finite-difference modification of the Hamiltonian? The paper asks whether choices of polymerization function correspond to undetermined higher-curvature terms in a covariant action.

sources.title: Singularity avoidance in quantum gravity

evidence.text: Can quantum-gravity higher-curvature terms relax geodesic focusing and singularity-theorem conditions? The paper distinguishes nonperturbative quadratic gravity from general relativity treated perturbatively as an effective field theory.

sources.title: The String Landscape, the Swampland, and the Missing Corner

evidence.text: Can quantum gravity have a direct microscopic bulk formulation that describes geometry and topology fluctuations while recovering smooth spacetime, rather than accessing the bulk only through strongly coupled boundary variables?

sources.title: Emergence of Weak Coupling at Large Distance in Quantum Gravity

evidence.text: What restrictions does quantum gravity impose on continuous parameters and asymptotic scalar-field geometry? The imported conjectures connect scalar expectation values, infinite moduli-space diameter, and towers becoming exponentially light with geodesic distance.

evidence.text: How can the group structure of stabilizer codes support quantum error correction, efficient encoding, fault-tolerant computation, and bounds on code efficiency and channel capacity? The thesis combines an overview with constructions and calculations.

sources.title: Stabilizer codes and quantum error correction

evidence.text: Code bounds use weight enumerators for S and N(S), the quantum MacWilliams identity, shadow-enumerator positivity, and linear programming. The paper states that the enumerator identities extend beyond stabilizer codes. Its separate treatment of low-weight degeneracy counts orthogonal error states inside subspaces fixed by low-weight stabilizers.

sources.title: Stabilizer codes and quantum error correction

evidence.text: Gaussian elimination using generator multiplication and qubit rearrangement produces a stabilizer standard form. Controlled Pauli operations and Hadamards then give an encoder with at most r one-qubit operations and n(n−k) two-qubit operations, where r is the binary X-part rank. Reversing this encoder decodes after an error-correction cycle.

sources.title: Stabilizer codes and quantum error correction

evidence.text: Represent stabilizer generators by binary rows (a|b), dropping overall phases. Commutation is encoded by Q((a|b),(c|d)) = Σ_i(a_i d_i+b_i c_i) = 0 modulo two. An alternative additive GF(4) representation uses X→1, Z→ω, Y→ω²; GF(4) linearity additionally requires closure under multiplication by ω.

destination.question: How do vacuum energy, quantum-state prescriptions and cosmological dynamics affect the existence, evolution, continuation and probabilistic interpretation of cosmological histories, under their stated conditions of control?
destination.summary: The original numerical membership supplies provenance but no independently established scientific boundary. Useful directions concern vacuum construction, radiative matching, persistence, transitions, initial conditions, nonsingular evolution and cosmological inference. These directions can share sources without sharing assumptions or canonical question identity. The child batches remain provenance records rather than five mandatory public branches.

systems: Quantum fields and effective theories coupled to gravity
String compactifications and proposed quantum descriptions of cosmological vacua
Vacuum bubbles, walls and higher-dimensional constructions
targets: Vacuum existence, stabilization and calculational control
Definition, matching and radiative sensitivity of vacuum energy
Persistence, transition probabilities and spacetime evolution
Preparation, weighting and continuation of cosmological histories
Perturbations, gravitational response and possible observational discrimination
Justification of cosmological probability and selection assumptions
regimes: Positive, zero and negative vacuum energies where specified
Stationary vacua and evolving cosmological backgrounds
Classical, semiclassical and proposed quantum descriptions
Local transition intervals and complete histories
Source-specific dimensions, curvature and observer locations
Early, late, finite-duration and asymptotic cosmology
assumptions: Quantum-gravity conjectures remain conditional and source-specific
Construction, stability, population and observational viability are separate tests
A local controlled interval does not establish a complete cosmological history
Observer conditioning does not establish a physical sampling process
Child-ledger coverage is attributed evidence, not a parent rereading of descendants
conventions: Distinguish a running vacuum coefficient, the full effective potential and a stable gravitational solution
Distinguish cosmological bounces from Euclidean tunneling bounces
Retain frames, curvature assumptions, fluctuation prescriptions and boundary conditions
Distinguish wall observers, bubble-interior observers and bulk geometry
Preserve source dates and original reading limits
includes: Conditional constructions, critiques and nonpositive results
Method and comparison routes to gravitational probes and inference questions
excludes: Numerical ancestry as proof of scientific equivalence
A universal de Sitter prohibition or universal NEC-instability theorem
Identification of every effective solution with a state of one quantum theory
Admission of unresolved child scopes through parent inclusion
Present-day observational validation inferred from historical descriptions

sources.title: Unitary null energy condition violation in P(X) cosmologies

evidence.text: Can a single scalar produce NEC violation and an Einstein-frame cosmological bounce while its fluctuations remain classically stable and below their perturbative strong-coupling scale? The focus is on P(Φ,X) theories and whether higher-energy irrelevant operators open a controlled window.

sources.title: de Sitter decay through goldstino evaporation

evidence.text: Which conjectural quantum-gravity restrictions motivate an instability of apparently metastable de Sitter EFT vacua? The paper distinguishes scalar-potential restrictions from conjectures that can allow de Sitter provided its lifetime is short.

sources.title: Wilsonian Effective Field Theory and String Theory

evidence.text: Does the sign of a string-derived ultraviolet vacuum energy constrain the sign of the cosmological vacuum energy after integrating all lower-energy fluctuations? The question requires specified matching data, particle thresholds and a distinction between a running coupling and the full effective potential.

sources.title: Disturbing implications of a cosmological constant

evidence.text: Can conventional quantum mechanics, holography and horizon complementarity in a universe with a fundamental positive cosmological constant explain, or at least accommodate, an inflationary low-entropy beginning and the observed kind of cosmological history?

sources.title: k-Essence, superluminal propagation, causality and emergent geometry

evidence.text: Can a regular positive-kinetic background evolve through the NEC boundary? The proposed obstruction is quantum excitation near singular acoustic geometry, extending earlier cosmological arguments.

sources.title: k-Essence, superluminal propagation, causality and emergent geometry

evidence.text: Does a growing Fourier solution in moving coordinates demonstrate instability of the preferred-frame retarded response? The appendix compares kernels constructed with two different definitions of retardation and finds that they agree only on the slow branch.

sources.title: Lectures on Cosmic Inflation and its Potential Stringy Realizations

evidence.text: What minimal field dynamics can keep the universe approximately vacuum dominated and later allow the field to evolve away?

sources.title: Lectures on Cosmic Inflation and its Potential Stringy Realizations

evidence.text: Can an earlier accelerating epoch dynamically prepare the spatial flatness and causal correlations required by the later hot Big Bang?

sources.title: Lectures on Cosmic Inflation and its Potential Stringy Realizations

evidence.text: Why must an expanding hot Big Bang begin extraordinarily close to spatial flatness to remain nearly flat today?

sources.title: Lectures on Cosmic Inflation and its Potential Stringy Realizations

evidence.text: How did widely separated last-scattering regions acquire nearly equal temperatures if the decelerating hot Big Bang supplied insufficient causal contact?

sources.title: Smallness of the cosmological constant and the multiple point principle

evidence.text: Can a tiny energy generated in a second phase explain the observed positive vacuum energy of the physical phase?

sources.title: TASI Lectures on the Cosmological Constant

evidence.text: What principle, dynamics, boundary condition, or environmental selection explains a total vacuum density many orders below its estimated field-theory contributions? Any proposed explanation must also permit the observed matter, radiation, and cosmic history.

sources.title: Power of Black Hole Physics: Seeing through the Vacuum Landscape

evidence.text: Can black-hole species constraints restrict de Sitter and slow-roll states connected to our vacuum, including their curvature, lifetime and allowed scalar-field deformations? Can many possible decay channels substantially shorten metastable-vacuum lifetimes?

sources.title: Everything You Always Wanted To Know About The Cosmological Constant Problem (But Were Afraid To Ask)

evidence.text: How should classical and quantum vacuum contributions to the cosmological constant be defined and renormalized, and why does a discrepancy with gravitational observations remain after divergences are removed?

sources.title: The Cosmological Constant Problem: Why it's hard to get Dark Energy from Micro-physics

evidence.text: Why does quantum vacuum energy produce so little observed curvature, and can its small gravitational effect be technically natural? The focus is the old cosmological constant problem, distinguished from explaining the observed nonzero value or cosmic coincidence.

sources.title: Quantum Exclusion of Positive Cosmological Constant?

evidence.text: Can a strictly constant positive vacuum-energy source remain consistent with a finite-occupation quantum-corpuscular description of de Sitter, and for how long can its classical GR mean field survive?

sources.title: Quantum Cosmology in Four Dimensions

evidence.text: How do anomalous gravitational dressings in a proposed four-dimensional nonlocal effective action modify homogeneous cosmology, and can the resulting vacuum-energy decay drive slow-roll expansion without an inflaton?

sources.title: Could LIV/noncommutativity alleviate the cosmological constant problem?

evidence.text: Can Lorentz-invariance violation or noncommutative spacetime models soften the ultraviolet behavior of scalar vacuum energy enough to mitigate the cosmological constant problem?

sources.title: Damped perturbations in the no-boundary state

evidence.text: Does an exactly evaluated, nonlinearly anisotropic minisuperspace implementation of the no-boundary path integral yield a physically acceptable state with damped perturbations? The paper examines how initial momentum regularity and the complex lapse contour affect disputed enhancement of anisotropies.

sources.title: De Sitter Space and the Swampland

evidence.text: Can a local scalar excitation prepare a causally isolated accelerating region inside an initially smooth asymptotically flat universe?

sources.title: Bounds on Slow Roll and the de Sitter Swampland

evidence.text: Does consistent quantum gravity forbid positive-energy de Sitter vacua or sustained potential slow roll? The paper investigates this question through restricted tree-level string compactifications while recognizing that their evidential scope is narrower than a universal quantum-gravity principle.

sources.title: The quantum swampland

evidence.text: Can quantum-state consistency obstruct metastable de Sitter space even when an effective potential appears stabilized? The paper answers conjecturally through unavoidable particle production and backreaction.

sources.title: The quantum swampland

evidence.text: Can balancing classical contributions against quantum loops produce metastable de Sitter space? A correction can be perturbatively small for moduli stability yet dominate the residual cosmological constant after cancellations.

sources.title: Bounds on Slow Roll at the Boundary of the Landscape

evidence.text: Do potential slow-roll obstructions exclude quantum de Sitter vacua, or characterize the tree-level boundary of the string landscape? A separate issue is whether families of solutions can approach arbitrarily weak coupling while retaining de Sitter.

sources.title: Why The Cosmological Constant is a Boundary Condition

evidence.text: Why should the cosmological constant be treated as an infrared boundary condition defining a quantum-gravity model, and where does the conventional bulk vacuum-energy calculation exceed the validity of quantum field theory?

sources.title: Quintessence Axion Revisited in Light of Swampland Conjectures

evidence.text: Can the vacuum structure associated with a fixed electroweak theta angle coexist with conjectural restrictions on stable de Sitter and nonsupersymmetric AdS vacua? The paper uses the refined de Sitter formulation and explicitly qualifies the treatment of negative-energy minima.

sources.title: Open problems on classical de Sitter solutions

evidence.text: Does difficulty finding de Sitter solutions in an asymptotic large-field limit exclude a finite but controlled anisotropic regime?

sources.title: The Swampland: Introduction and Review

evidence.text: Can a positive-energy string vacuum survive the consistency and control tests required of a quantum-gravity solution? Positive maxima and metastable minima test different versions of the de Sitter conjectures.

sources.title: Some remarks on Swampland conjectures, fluxes and K-theory in IIB toroidal compactifications

evidence.text: Are the proposed dS states short-lived enough for the intended censorship constraint once instantonic transitions and ordinary vacuum decay are included?

sources.title: On the Limits of Effective Quantum Field Theory: Eternal Inflation, Landscapes, and Other Mythical Beasts

evidence.text: Which cosmological properties are imposed rather than explained by initial-state selection? This HST construction assumes flatness, homogeneity, and isotropy while allowing states subject to overlap consistency.

sources.title: k-Essence, superluminal propagation, causality and emergent geometry

evidence.text: Match the principal and first-derivative parts of the scalar operator to an emergent covariant d'Alembertian. Solve for its conformal normalization using the determinant and derivative-Hessian identities.

sources.title: Lectures on Cosmic Inflation and its Potential Stringy Realizations

evidence.text: Specify component equations of state and initial densities, integrate conservation separately, sum densities, and integrate the Friedmann equation. Equality epochs follow by equating component densities rather than by assuming continued single-component dominance through the transition.

sources.title: Smallness of the cosmological constant and the multiple point principle

evidence.text: Run the physical coupling from M_Z to M_S, match the two phase couplings, and evolve the second phase to the formal zero of its inverse coupling. Change the beta coefficient whenever the light matter spectrum changes.

sources.title: TASI Lectures on the Cosmological Constant

evidence.text: Approximate a thin energy shell by its continuum volume and compare that volume with a lattice cell. The operation estimates configuration abundance, with arithmetic and degeneracy checks needed for claims about actual nearby energy levels.

sources.title: Power of Black Hole Physics: Seeing through the Vacuum Landscape

evidence.text: Vacuum-decay estimates use semiclassical instanton rates, sums over channels and a dilute-gas-like multi-instanton model. Flux-transition estimates use supergravity extrema and domain-wall tension related to a central function.

sources.title: Everything You Always Wanted To Know About The Cosmological Constant Problem (But Were Afraid To Ask)

evidence.text: The Gaussian effective potential minimizes a Gaussian state's energy over its width at fixed mean field. A gap equation determines the variational mass; derivatives of the potential at zero field define renormalized mass and quartic coupling.

sources.title: Emergent de Sitter Cosmology from Decaying Anti–de Sitter Space

evidence.text: Can positive-energy 4D FLRW cosmology and effective gravity emerge on an expanding decay bubble in AdS, without requiring a fundamental de Sitter vacuum or a scale-separated compactification?

sources.title: Are we typical?

evidence.text: What warrants a typicality assumption: observed populations, a conjectured prediction, or preference? The source separates these grounds and emphasizes that choosing a class already affects whether humans appear typical.
